slides.title: Wahaj Electricity Distribution Company runs three systems in production
slides.text: One case study all week Wahaj Electricity Distribution Company runs three systems in production A fictional distributor: six regions, 4,800 feeders, crews in the field and a control room. You operate: Fault-risk classifier Scores every feeder monthly; the top of the list is inspected first. Retrained on monthly batches. Nabd نبض The field-crew assistant: retrieval over the maintenance manuals and two tools. Mubadir مبادر The outage-ticket agent: finds the customer, checks the outage, opens or closes tickets.

slides.title: Operate with evidence, on free hosted models, with AI as a tutor
slides.text: How this course works Operate with evidence, on free hosted models, with AI as a tutor Evidence first Every release decision in the labs is taken on a log, a metric or a trace, and written down. No model on your laptop Language model labs call a free hosted model, or a scripted stand-in when no key works. Training runs on a laptop processor or Colab. AI as a tutor An assistant may explain logs and give hints. It does not write your pipeline or alert definitions. Supervised checks. The entry and exit checks are done without AI: reading a pipeline log and a trace, and choosing a rollback trigger.

slides.title: An alias is a pointer that the provider can move
slides.text: Provider model identifiers An alias is a pointer that the provider can move run A asked hosted/steady-latest answered by hosted/steady-2026-09-12 run B asked hosted/steady-latest answered by hosted/steady-2026-10-14 Release files that name the alias look identical on both dates. The response says which model answered: record that field on every call. Pin a dated identifier in the release, and change it only through a release.

slides.title: The manifest hashes every part; its own id is the hash of all of them
slides.text: Lab 1.1 · steps 2 and 3 The manifest hashes every part; its own id is the hash of all of them parts = { "classifier": {"registry": "fault-risk@champion v3", "threshold": 0.35, ...}, "nabd": {"prompt": sha("prompt.txt"), "tools": sha("tools.json"), "index": "v3", "index_fingerprint": Index("v3").fingerprint(), "model_requested": rel["model"], "model_resolved": log["response_model"]}, "mubadir": {f: sha(f) for f in bundle_files}, } release_id = "wahaj-" + sha_json(parts)[:12]

slides.text: Session 2 Registries and lineage Read a model version, its alias and its lineage tags Rebuild a data snapshot from its content hash Reproduce a colleague's model and prove it matches 02

slides.title: A registry holds versions; an alias says which version does which job
slides.text: Recap from AE-205 A registry holds versions; an alias says which version does which job Version Immutable: one trained model, its run, its metrics. Alias Mutable: champion, challenger-b. Serving loads models:/fault-risk@champion. Tags The lineage: data snapshot, code hash, months, author, the reason for a promotion.

slides.title: Follow the champion back to the exact data and code
slides.text: Lineage Follow the champion back to the exact data and code Alias champion → Version 3 registered in August → Run parameters and metrics → Snapshot de8fd6c3… (32,400 rows) → Code trainer hash Reproduce before you trust. A registry entry that cannot be rebuilt is a file with a name.

slides.title: Name the data by its content, as DVC and lakeFS do
slides.text: Data versioning Name the data by its content, as DVC and lakeFS do data = df.to_csv(index=False).encode() h = sha256(data) path = store / h[:2] / f"{h}.csv" if not path.exists(): path.write_bytes(data) The same rows give the same name on any machine. A file called training_latest.csv says nothing about which rows it held last month. The tools add remote storage, branches and garbage collection; the idea is this one line.

slides.title: Parameters come back from the tracking store as text
slides.text: A trap in Lab 1.2 Parameters come back from the tracking store as text params {"max_iter": "150", "learning_rate": "0.05", "recent_weight": "4"} retrain TypeError, or worse, a silent change of meaning Convert on purpose Keep a typed list of the training parameters and convert each one when you read it back.

slides.title: A reproduction matches on data hash, code hash and every prediction
slides.text: Lab 1.2 · step 4 A reproduction matches on data hash, code hash and every prediction = snapshot hash rebuilt from the months = training code hash 0.0 largest difference in predicted risk on 1,200 holdout feeders The same code on "the latest training file" (up to August) gives another hash and predictions that differ by up to half the scale.

slides.title: The library versions are part of the release too
slides.text: What lineage still misses The library versions are part of the release too The same code and data on another scikit-learn version can give different trees. labs/uv.lock pins every package; the capstone repository commits its own lock file. A container image digest pins the operating system and Python as well (AE-205). In Colab the libraries are Colab's, so a rebuild there can differ from your laptop's by a few thousandths: that difference is an environment change, and now you can name it.

slides.title: Reproduced, or just similar?
slides.text: Checkpoint Reproduced, or just similar? You retrain Lamya's model from the shared training file and get the same AUC to three decimals, but the data hash differs from the registry tag. What do you conclude? It is reproduced: the AUC matches The hash function is unreliable across machines Update the registry tag to the new hash It is a different model: rebuild the snapshot from the months in the lineage

slides.title: Pipelines with validation
slides.text: Session 3 Pipelines with validation Write a data contract as a schema with types, ranges and allowed values Add batch checks: row count and duplicate keys Make validation a pipeline step that stops the run with a report 03

slides.title: A broken batch trains without an error
slides.text: The September batch A broken batch trains without an error Al-Hadba's load arrived as a fraction: feeder F-0801 reads 0.815, not 81.5. 36 rows arrived twice. 14 Al-Sahil rows carry the code "SAH ", with a trailing space. Training does not complain Every value is a valid number or string. The model learns that Al-Hadba never has load, and its metric on the same broken data can look fine.

slides.title: A contract says what every row and every batch must be
slides.text: Data contracts A contract says what every row and every batch must be Row rules Types, patterns (^F-\d{4}$), allowed values, physical ranges (load 20 to 150 percent of rating), no nulls. Batch rules One row per feeder, every feeder present (within 2%), the month the file claims. Agree it with the data owner. The SCADA export team signs the contract; your pipeline enforces it on every delivery.

slides.title: The contract as a pandera schema
slides.text: Lab 1.3 · step 1 The contract as a pandera schema import pandera.pandas as pa SCHEMA = pa.DataFrameSchema({ "feeder_id": pa.Column(str, pa.Check.str_matches(r"^F-\d{4}$")), "region": pa.Column(str, pa.Check.isin(["RIM", "HAD", "SAH", "WAD", "JAB", "NAK"])), "load_peak_pct": pa.Column(float, pa.Check.in_range(20, 150)), "fault_30d": pa.Column(int, pa.Check.isin([0, 1])), ... }, strict=True) SCHEMA.validate(df, lazy=True) # every failure, not the first

slides.text: Lab 1.3 · step 3 Validation is a step that can stop the run load the batch → validate contract and batch rules → train only if valid → gate Session 4 A failed validation raises a stop, writes a report, and leaves the champion untouched. An orchestrator (Prefect, Airflow, Kubeflow Pipelines) records the run as stopped, not failed.

slides.title: Report the fault to the owner; do not quietly repair it
slides.text: What the pipeline must not do Report the fault to the owner; do not quietly repair it Quiet repairs Dropping duplicates, multiplying small loads by 100, stripping spaces: each hides a broken export that will break again. Stop, quarantine, report Keep the failing rows apart, send the counts and one example, retrain when the corrected batch arrives.

slides.title: Where does validation go?
slides.text: Checkpoint Where does validation go? A batch delivers one region's load as a fraction instead of a percentage. Where should the pipeline catch it? In a contract step before training, which stops the run and reports the column In the promotion gate, when the new model's AUC drops When crews complain about the inspection list In a cleaning step that multiplies values below 2 by 100

slides.title: Promotion gates
slides.text: Session 4 Promotion gates Score champion and challengers on the same holdout Compare overall and by region with a stated tolerance Promote by moving the registry alias, with the reason logged 04

slides.title: Salt fog started tripping coastal lines, and the champion had never seen it
slides.text: August in Al-Sahil Salt fog started tripping coastal lines, and the champion had never seen it From August, overhead feeders within 10 km of the coast fault far more often. The champion was trained on November to July: distance to the coast never mattered. Two challengers were trained in October on February to August. 0.742 champion's AUC in Al-Sahil on the August holdout (0.830 overall)

slides.title: A challenger is promoted only when it beats the champion on the same holdout
slides.text: Champion and challenger A challenger is promoted only when it beats the champion on the same holdout Same holdout The quarter of feeders no model trained on, in the newest month with complete labels. Overall Better than the champion's AUC. By region No region more than 0.03 worse. Why regions. Crews and customers live in regions. An average can hide a region that pays for everyone else's gain.

slides.title: Challenger A learned from labels that had not arrived yet
slides.text: The cause behind challenger A Challenger A learned from labels that had not arrived yet The first cut of the August batch came before the inspections of the most wooded Al-Jabal feeders were entered. Their faults read 0, so A learned that wooded mountain feeders are safe. The complete batch came three weeks later; challenger B was trained on it. A data problem, caught by a model gate No contract rule fails: 0 is a valid label. Only the regional comparison shows it.

slides.title: Promotion moves an alias, and the old champion stays one move away
slides.text: Lab 1.4 · step 4 Promotion moves an alias, and the old champion stays one move away old = client.get_model_version_by_alias("fault-risk", "champion").version new = client.get_model_version_by_alias("fault-risk", "challenger-b").version client.set_registered_model_alias("fault-risk", "previous-champion", old) client.set_registered_model_alias("fault-risk", "champion", new) client.set_model_version_tag("fault-risk", new, "promoted_reason", "passed overall and in every region (holdout 2026-08, tolerance 0.03)")

slides.title: A rule with no tolerance rejects every challenger on noise
slides.text: The tolerance A rule with no tolerance rejects every challenger on noise 200 holdout feeders per region, 16 to 81 of them with a fault in August. Resample them and a region's AUC moves by a few hundredths. Challenger B is at most 0.006 worse in any region (Al-Jabal): noise. A is 0.069 worse there: not noise. Stretch. Bootstrap the Al-Wadi gap of challenger B and read whether its interval includes zero.

slides.title: Better on average
slides.text: Checkpoint Better on average Challenger A beats the champion overall (0.851 against 0.830) and is 0.069 worse in Al-Jabal. The tolerance is 0.03. What happens? Promote it: the overall gain is larger than one region's loss Raise the tolerance to 0.07 for this release Reject it, record the region and the cause, and look at challenger B Use A everywhere except Al-Jabal

slides.title: Which part of the release unit changed?
slides.text: Review of Day 1 Which part of the release unit changed? The fault-risk model's registry version, threshold and code hash are unchanged, but its predictions on the same feeders differ from last week's. What do you check first? Nothing: the model version is the same, so it is noise Retrain and compare the AUC The input data and environment the predictions were made with Lower the promotion tolerance

slides.title: Continuous delivery for models
slides.text: Session 1 Continuous delivery for models Promote one artefact by digest instead of rebuilding it Add a staging check and an approval step before production Keep a deployment log a reviewer can audit 01

slides.title: Every push to main goes straight to production, rebuilt with the tag latest
slides.text: Where Wahaj starts Every push to main goes straight to production, rebuilt with the tag latest jobs: deploy: steps: - run: make test - run: docker build -t registry.wahaj.example/nabd:latest . - run: docker push registry.wahaj.example/nabd:latest - run: ./deploy.sh production registry.wahaj.example/nabd:latest Lab 2.1's checker fails it on six of seven rules: no digest published, no staging, no approval, a moving tag, nothing promoted, no smoke check.

slides.title: Build once; promote the same digest through every environment
slides.text: Continuous delivery for models Build once; promote the same digest through every environment Merge to main tests run → Build push, publish the digest → Staging deploy the digest, smoke check → Approval a reviewer, not the author → Production the same digest A rebuild is a new artefact. The same commit can pull a newer base image or package. Only the digest that passed staging goes on.

slides.title: The build job hands its digest to the jobs that deploy
slides.text: Lab 2.1 · step 2 The build job hands its digest to the jobs that deploy build: outputs: digest: ${{ steps.push.outputs.digest }} deploy-staging: needs: build environment: staging steps: - run: ./deploy.sh staging ${{ needs.build.outputs.digest }} - run: ./smoke_check.sh staging deploy-production: needs: [build, deploy-staging] environment: production

slides.title: The approval lives in the environment's protection rules, not in the file
slides.text: The approval step The approval lives in the environment's protection rules, not in the file Required reviewers: up to six people or teams; one approval lets the job start. Self-review can be blocked: Dhafer merged, so Mutab approves. A pull request cannot remove the rule by editing the workflow. Plan limits On GitHub's free plans, required reviewers work on public repositories only. The capstone repository is public.

slides.title: The release waits at production until a reviewer who did not merge approves
slides.text: Lab 2.1 · step 4, from the course's run The release waits at production until a reviewer who did not merge approves build built sha256:ce56953fe2d35ec1 staging deployed the digest · smoke check passed production waiting for approval approval Dhafer Al-Hazzani: refused, he merged the change production approved by Mutab Al-Shalhoub · deployed the same digest

slides.title: A rollback redeploys a recorded digest through the same gate
slides.text: The other direction A rollback redeploys a recorded digest through the same gate on: workflow_dispatch: inputs: digest: {required: true} jobs: rollback-production: environment: production steps: - run: ./deploy.sh production ${{ inputs.digest }} No build: the digest already passed once. The same reviewers approve it, so a rollback is also recorded. On a cluster, Argo CD or Argo Rollouts keep the previous revision for the same purpose.

slides.title: Approved, then rebuilt
slides.text: Checkpoint Approved, then rebuilt The production job checks out the approved commit, builds the image again and deploys it. Staging tested an image built from the same commit an hour earlier. What is wrong? Production may run an artefact nobody tested: it should deploy the digest staging tested Nothing: the same commit gives the same image Nothing: a reviewer approved the commit Only the build time: run both builds at once

slides.title: An index refresh changes what the model reads, so it is gated like a model
slides.text: The change people underestimate An index refresh changes what the model reads, so it is gated like a model A new manual can outrank the right section for an old question. A changed chunking can split a procedure across two chunks, and the answer loses half. Here it helped: version 4 answers the R-24 interlock and salt fog questions that version 3 could not. Refresh as a release. Rebuild, fingerprint, gate, then switch the alias the assistant reads. Day 3 Session 4 adds a policy for when to refresh.

slides.title: Shadow and canary on evidence
slides.text: Session 3 Shadow and canary on evidence Compare a candidate in shadow without user impact Analyse a canary window with a minimum sample Roll back automatically on a quality or latency trigger 03

slides.title: The offline set is fixed; real traffic changes through the day
slides.text: Why a canary after a gate The offline set is fixed; real traffic changes through the day The provider's snapshot steady-2026-10-14 passed Nabd's offline gate. The offline cases are mostly in English. Crews ask in both languages, and the mix moves with the shift. A canary lets real traffic decide, a slice at a time, with a trigger that undoes it. Recap from AE-205 Canary and rollback for a web service. Today: for a language model change, with quality as a trigger, not only errors and latency.

slides.title: Shadow risks nobody; a canary risks a few, on purpose
slides.text: Two ways to expose a candidate Shadow risks nobody; a canary risks a few, on purpose Shadow The candidate answers a copy of every request; users see only the stable answer. Double the tokens, no user impact. Canary A share of real users get the candidate: 5%, then 25%, then 50%. slides.title: The population stability index compares a day's distribution with a reference
slides.text: A drift statistic The population stability index compares a day's distribution with a reference edges = quantiles(reference, deciles) ref = share of reference per bin cur = share of today per bin psi = sum((cur - ref) * ln(cur / ref)) PSI Rule of thumb below 0.1 stable 0.1 to 0.25 a moderate move above 0.25 a large move

The session started over and opened a second ticket. Retry The ticket service committed, then timed out. The harness retried and wrote again.

slides.title: A checkpointer saves the state after every step, under a thread id
slides.text: Durable execution A checkpointer saves the state after every step, under a thread id g = StateGraph(Ticket) g.add_node("find_customer", find_customer) # ... get_outage, create_ticket, notify_crew g.add_edge(START, "find_customer") graph = g.compile(checkpointer=SqliteSaver(sqlite3.connect("checkpoints.db"))) graph.invoke({"account": "ACC-40000137"}, {"configurable": {"thread_id": "S-4202"}}) graph.invoke(None, {"configurable": {"thread_id": "S-4202"}}) # resume after a crash

slides.title: An idempotency key names one intended write; a repeat returns the first result
slides.text: Lab 4.2 · step 4 An idempotency key names one intended write; a repeat returns the first result key = hash(session_id, "create_ticket", args) # same intent, same key, on every retry # a different report gets a different key timeout after the commit retry OT-31001, replayed: true tickets one, notified

slides.title: Checkpoints protect the steps between calls; keys protect the call itself
slides.text: Which fix for which failure Checkpoints protect the steps between calls; keys protect the call itself Checkpoint The process dies between steps. Resume from the saved state; finished steps do not run again. Idempotency key The answer to one write is lost. Retry with the same key; the service does not write twice. Both, for every agent that writes. The capstone's agent incident is a duplicate write.

slides.text: Checkpoint Checkpointed, still duplicated Mubadir's flow now has a checkpointer. A ticket service timeout still produced two tickets for one report. Why? The checkpointer was not saving The ticket database lost the first ticket The retry ran inside one step, and the service had no key to recognise it The model asked for two tickets

slides.title: Replay from the recording, not a rerun against today's services
slides.text: Lab 4.3 · step 2 Replay from the recording, not a rerun against today's services The recording holds every model output and every tool response. Replay feeds them back through today's harness code: no model, no services. The same wrong answer comes back every time. A rerun would not The replica has caught up and a hosted model can answer differently: the failure would hide.

slides.title: A guard in the harness blocks a close on a stale status
slides.text: Lab 4.3 · step 3 A guard in the harness blocks a close on a stale status def freshness_guard(action, history): if action["tool"] != "close_report": return None last = latest get_outage result in history if last["status"] != "restored": return "not restored" if last["age_minutes"] > 15: return f"status is {last['age_minutes']} minutes old: confirm with the control room" Replayed with the guard: blocked at step 3, "status is 140 minutes old (limit 15)".
